species.habitat: Forest edges, woodlands, suburban parks & gardens
species.fun_fact: Robins can hear earthworms moving underground by tilting their heads to align their ears!
species.touch_grass_tip: Look up in open deciduous branch forks or near grassy trail clearings.

species.habitat: Dense shrubbery, forest margins, overgrown thickets
species.fun_fact: Both male and female cardinals sing, which is rare among North American songbirds!
species.touch_grass_tip: Scan low thickets and evergreen tangles about 5 to 10 feet off the trail ground.

species.habitat: Deciduous and mixed forests, trail edges, willow thickets
species.fun_fact: The number of 'dee' notes at the end of their alarm call indicates the level of threat from a predator!
species.touch_grass_tip: Pause silently under birch or pine trees; chickadees are curious and will hop close to inspect you.

species.habitat: Oak-hickory forests, pine woodlands, park boundaries
species.fun_fact: Blue Jays are famous mimics! They frequently imitate hawk calls to test if real hawks are nearby or to clear out bird feeders.
species.touch_grass_tip: Listen for alarm calls high in oak treetops, especially near acorn drops.

species.habitat: Brushy fields, wetland borders, trail reedy edges
species.fun_fact: Male song sparrows learn their complex songs from neighboring males during their first summer!
species.touch_grass_tip: Look at exposed perches on high reeds or fenceposts near trail water crossings.

species.habitat: Open fields, trail gravel paths, telephone wires
species.fun_fact: Their wings make a sharp whistling noise on takeoff to alert flock members of sudden motion!
species.touch_grass_tip: Look along gravel trail edges where they forage for fallen seeds.

species.call_pattern: wild laugh call / heavy wood drum
species.habitat: Mature deep forests with large dead standing trees
species.fun_fact: Their excavations create rectangular holes so large they can weaken small dead trees, providing shelter for owls and bats!
species.touch_grass_tip: Follow the sound of heavy hollow thumping into old-growth timber stands.
